texts.facts: Benefit u/s 428 Cr.P.C. also given to the appellant. The brief facts of the present case are that on 20.06.2019, at about 02:45 pm, Food Inspector (FI) Sanjeev Kumar Gupta and Sh. Mittar Pal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. R.K. Sharma visited the Kiran byDate:Kiran Gupta Gupta 2024.07.03 15:15:57 +0530 premises of M/s Baniya General Store, Shop No. 315, Main Bazaar, Subzi Mandi, Delhi-110007 where the appellants were found conducting business of various food articles including 'ghee', which were lying stored for sale for human consumption in open aluminum tub bearing no label declaration. The sample was seized as per rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI alongwith Panchnama etc. was prepared at the spot. Thereafter, one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. That vide report dated 06.07.2009, the PA found the sample to be substandard not confirming to the standards on the grounds that the BR reading exceeded the prescribed maximum Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/ 2 limit of 43 and the Reichert value was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 28. It also gave a positive B.T. test which should be negative in ghee. Subsequently, on the basis of the report, the present complaint was filed against the appellant and his father Sh. Raj Kumar. During trial, Sh. Raj Kumar expired and proceedings against him were abated vide order dated 30.01.2020. Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date: Gupta 2024.07.03 15:16:02 +0530 4. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the appellant alongwith his father was summoned vide order dated 23.11.2019. After recording, pre-charge evidence, vide order dated 12.05.2010 charge u/s 16(1)(a) and 16(1)(c) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act was framed against the appellant to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. The prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 is FI Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, he in his testimony exhibited the documents Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/L and Mark X. PW-2 is Sh. R.K. Sharma (SDM/LHA). He deposed on similar lines as PW1 and identified his signatures on relevant documents. PW-3 Sh. Mittar Pal, Retd. FA, deposed that on the request of PW1 he joined the sample proceedings. He relied upon the pamphlet Ex.PW1/A1 and his signatures on Ex.PW1/D1. All these witnesses were duly cross-examined. 6. The statement of appellant was recorded under Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date: Gupta 2024.07.03 15:16:08 +0530 section 313 Cr.P.C. on 09.12.2013 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. He stated that the present complaint was filed because his father / co-accused had given complaint against nearby shopkeepers who were indulging in food adulteration. He in his defence, examined himself as DW3 and two witnesses - DW-1 Sh. Rajesh & DW-2 Sh. Laxmi Narain. These witnesses were duly cross examined by ld. SPP. GROUNDS OF APPEAL Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/ 3 7. The appellant has taken the following grounds of appeal. The PA report was received on 06.07.2009 by the respondent and prosecution was instituted much lateron 23.11.2009. It is prayed that in view of grounds of appeal, the impugned judgment dated 17.10.2022 and order on the point of sentence dated 20.10.2022 may kindly be [LEAKAGE_MASK].
texts.arguments: The Ld. Counsel for the appellant has stated that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the witnesses deposed before the court were against the facts and contradictory to each other. Though the appellant has taken the said ground, however, he has nowhere described as to how and in which manner the deposition of witnesses were against the facts or contrary to each other. In fact, the Ld. ACMM in para 20 of the judgment has discussed the contradictions which were argued by ld. Counsel for appellant before her and rightly held that the said contradictions do not constitute material contradictions and are formal in nature. 9. Though the appellant has contended that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the respondent has not complied with the mandatory procedures and rules under the Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date: Gupta 2024.07.03 15:16:32 +0530 Act, however, he has failed to point out any such Rule or violation of the procedure by the respondent. Under S. 16(1)(a) minimum sentence of imprisonment is given. On this issue, Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr. Vs. The State of Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date: Gupta 2024.07.03 15:16:55 +0530 West Bengal & Ors, Special Leave Petition(Criminal) No.6095 of 2018, dated 07.03.2024, has observed that: "Whether the appellant can be granted the benefit of the new legislation and be awarded a lesser punishment as is presently prescribed under the new law. This court in T. Barai VS. Henry Ah Hoe (1983) 1 SCC 177, had held that when an amendment is beneficial to the accused it can be applied even to cases pending the courts where such a provision did not exist at the time of commission of offence." 15. The recent judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr. (Supra) has made it clear that if there is an amendment in the Act, which is beneficial to the accused, it can be applied even to the pending cases in the court where such provision was not in existence. The ratio of judgment M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr. (Supra) is squarely applicable to the facts of present case.
